question.text: Will COP31 in Antalya close more than 24 hours after its scheduled end?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if the final closing plenary of COP31 is gavelled closed after 18:00 Turkey time (UTC+3) on Saturday, November 21, 2026.

The closing time will be taken from the [IISD Earth Negotiations Bulletin](https://enb.iisd.org/) summary of COP31, or failing that from [UNFCCC](https://unfccc.int/cop31) webcast records or [credible](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) media reports.
question.fine_print:
* "Final closing plenary" means the last of the closing plenaries of the COP, CMP and CMA sessions to be held in Antalya. If any of the COP, CMP or CMA sessions are formally concluded without a closing plenary being held, the question will resolve according to the date and time of their formal conclusion, as recorded by the primary resolution sources.
* If COP31 is suspended or adjourned for a period of 14 days or more, the question will resolve according to the date and time that the suspension or adjournment occurred. But if COP31 is suspended or adjourned for a period of less than 14 days, the question will resolve according to the date and time of the final closing plenary.
* If COP31 does not begin in November 2026, the question will be **annulled**.

***
This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46106) which opened on 2026-11-02 18:00:00. This question will resolve based on the resolution criteria and fine print of the linked original question. However, if this question would resolve differently than the original question, then this question will be annulled. Additionally, if the original question's resolution could have been known before this question opened, then this question will be annulled.

research:
I couldn't find anything that settles this yet. COP31 opens on 2026-11-09, and its scheduled end is Friday 20 November. The threshold, 18:00 Turkey time on Saturday 21 November, is exactly 24 hours after the usual 18:00 Friday finish. Recent COPs have usually gone past 24 hours, but some have finished only a little under or over that line.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-08: The ENB site (enb.iisd.org) returned HTTP 403 when I tried to fetch it, so I couldn't check for a COP31 page. ENB summaries only come out after a session closes, so there's nothing to resolve on yet. [ENB](https://enb.iisd.org/)
- For reference, ENB's COP29 summary was the main record of that session's closing. [ENB COP29](https://enb.iisd.org/baku-un-climate-change-conference-cop29-summary)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-11-08: The conference hasn't started. It runs 9 to 20 November, with the leaders' summit on 11 to 12 November. Nothing settles the question yet. [AA](https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/ekonomi/cop31-alani-ve-yapilari-antalyanin-marka-degerini-guclendirecek/4114462)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-08: Road closures delayed 8 of the 21 shuttle routes the day before the opening. [Evrensel](https://www.evrensel.net/haber/6008526/cop31-katilimcilari-yolda-kaldi)
- 2026-11-07: Schools in seven Antalya districts move to remote learning on 11 to 12 November for leaders' summit security. [BirGün](https://www.birgun.net/haber/antalya-valiligi-duyurdu-cop31-icin-7-ilcede-2-gun-uzaktan-egitime-gecilecek-745088)
- 2026-11-05: Climate Home's preview lists the likely fights:
  - African countries and Nepal want extra agenda items, and Australia hopes to avoid an agenda fight at the opening plenary.
  - Other disputed topics: fossil-fuel references in the cover decision, the mitigation work programme, the timing of the next IPCC reports (AR7), the just transition mechanism, a number for adaptation finance, and trade.
  - The preview says nothing about a plan to finish on time. [Climate Home](https://www.climatechangenews.com/2026/11/05/cop31-briefing-what-to-expect-from-the-antalya-climate-summit/)
- Undated preview: if the agenda fight drags on, the opening days go to procedure. [Climate & Capital](https://www.climateandcapitalmedia.com/cop31-antalya-preview/)
- Leadership is split, which is unusual. Türkiye's Murat Kurum is COP president, while Australia's Chris Bowen runs the negotiations, drafts the texts and issues the final decision. Türkiye insists it will have the final say. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_Nations_Climate_Change_Conference), [Climate Home](https://www.climatechangenews.com/2026/11/05/cop31-briefing-what-to-expect-from-the-antalya-climate-summit/)
- A senior EU official says "We cannot expect a revolution" from Antalya, and a Carbon Pulse headline calls the carbon-market (Article 6) talks "low drama". [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/science/articles/cop31-faces-tough-test-climate-125430446.html), [Carbon Pulse](https://carbon-pulse.com/568111/?site=nzp)

## 4. Base rates
- 2025-11-22: COP30 in Belém officially finished at 8:44pm on Saturday. Carbon Brief puts that almost 27 hours past a 6pm Friday close, which would count as Yes, but only by about 2.7 hours. The closing plenary started about 3 hours late. [Carbon Brief](https://www.carbonbrief.org/cop30-key-outcomes-agreed-at-the-un-climate-talks-in-belem/)
- 2024-11-24: COP29 in Baku ended early Sunday, more than 30 hours late (sources say 30 to 36). [Belga](https://www.belganewsagency.eu/cop29--un-climate-summit-goes-into-overtime)
- 2023-12-13: COP28 in Dubai ended Wednesday morning, "nearly 24 hours" late according to Imperial. Carbon Brief ranked it only 13th-longest, below COP30. It was probably just under the 24-hour line, but I couldn't confirm the exact closing time. [Imperial](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/stories/cop28-imperial-researchers-reflect)
- COP25 in Madrid (2019) ran about 40 to 44 hours late, the longest ever. COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh (2022) ran about a day and a half late. [search summary](https://www.brusselstimes.com/1849266/climate-summit-goes-into-extra-time-as-usual)
- 2023-12-08: Carbon Brief found that 8 of the previous 10 COPs (COP18 to COP27) ran more than 24 hours over. No COP has finished roughly on time since COP12 in 2006. [Carbon Brief](https://carbonbrief.org/cop28-debriefed-8-december-the-fight-over-fossil-fuels-al-jaber-defends-respect-for-science-has-cop-ever-finished-on-time)
- Adding COP28 (probably under) and COP29 and COP30 (over) gives roughly 10 of the last 13 over 24 hours. The usual overrun is about 24 to 44 hours, often landing on Saturday evening, which is close to this question's threshold.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I couldn't find a Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on when COP31 will close. None of the market prices you collected are relevant: they cover DOGE, HYPE, Bitcoin, Solana, silver, OpenAI market share, the next Pope, a US-China trade deal, Canada-EU talks and prediction-market regulation.
- The only related Manifold market asks whether China, India or the US will sign the "35 by 35" pledge. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/FrankfurtSchool/ci2026-will-either-china-india-or-t)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-09: Opening plenaries. Watch whether the agenda is adopted without a fight over the African Group and Nepal items.
- 2026-11-10: Energy Day and the launch of the electrification pledge.
- 2026-11-11 to 12: World Leaders' Summit.
- Around 2026-11-14 to 15: Technical bodies (SB65) conclude, and drafts move to the ministerial stage.
- 2026-11-18 to 20: Draft cover decision texts are published. How late they appear has predicted overruns before; at COP30 the final text came out on Saturday morning.
- 2026-11-20: Scheduled close. 2026-11-21 18:00 Turkey time (UTC+3) is the threshold.

- Schedule: Antalya, 9 to 20 November 2026. Türkiye holds the presidency and Australia (Chris Bowen) leads the negotiations. [DCCEEW](https://www.dcceew.gov.au/climate-change/international-climate-action/unfccc-cop/cop31), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_Nations_Climate_Change_Conference)
- The threshold of Saturday 21 November at 18:00 Turkey time is 24 hours after the usual 18:00 Friday close.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The talks have not started yet.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-08: Road closures delayed 8 of 21 delegate shuttle routes the day before the opening. This is a logistics problem only. [Evrensel](https://www.evrensel.net/haber/6008526/cop31-katilimcilari-yolda-kaldi)
- 2026-11-07: Schools in seven Antalya districts will teach remotely on 11 and 12 November for the Leaders' Summit. The governorate still describes the conference as running 9 to 20 November. [Sabah](https://www.sabah.com.tr/yasam/antalyada-11-12-kasimda-okullar-tatil-mi-7-ilcede-egitim-karari-7696875)
- 2026-11-05: Climate Home's briefing points to several pressure points:
  - The split presidency carries risk if the two teams disagree on how the talks are going. Türkiye insists it will have the "final decision", and both teams plan to produce a cover decision.
  - Australia wants to avoid a fight over the agenda at the opening plenary. African countries and Nepal have asked for extra items.
  - Contested files include references to the fossil-fuel roadmap, the target for adaptation finance, a trade agenda item, the IPCC timeline and the scope of the just transition mechanism.
  - After the Bonn session in June failed to agree even minimal conclusions, the briefing says the forum's own future is in question.
  - Leader turnout looks low-key.
  - The article does not predict an overrun. [Climate Home](https://www.climatechangenews.com/2026/11/05/cop31-briefing-what-to-expect-from-the-antalya-climate-summit/)

## 4. Base rates
Overrun means hours past the scheduled close, usually 18:00 on the final day. Anything over 24 hours would count as Yes.
- 2025-11-22, COP30 Belém: officially finished at 20:44 on Saturday, about 27 hours late. Carbon Brief ranks it the 11th-longest COP, which means at least 10 earlier COPs overran by more than 27 hours. The closing plenary had started more than 2 hours late and was suspended for about an hour. [Carbon Brief](https://www.carbonbrief.org/cop30-key-outcomes-agreed-at-the-un-climate-talks-in-belem), [Carbon Brief DeBriefed](https://www.carbonbrief.org/debriefed-28-november-2025-cop30s-frustrating-end-asia-floods-uk-emergency-climate-event/), [Devex](https://www.devex.com/news/the-3-big-outcomes-of-cop30-s-final-plenary-111426)
- 2024-11-24, COP29 Baku: closed early Sunday, about 33 to 35 hours late. **Yes.** [search summary](https://carbonbrief.org/daily-brief/huge-cop29-climate-deal-too-little-too-late-poorer-nations-say)
- 2023-12-13, COP28 Dubai: the scheduled close was Tuesday 12 December. From memory, unverified: it closed around midday Wednesday, roughly 24 to 26 hours late. That is borderline.
- 2022-11-20, COP27 Sharm el-Sheikh: closed Sunday morning, about 40 hours late. **Yes** (from memory).
- 2021-11-13, COP26 Glasgow: about 24 hours late, closing on Saturday evening. That is borderline to Yes. [search summary](https://climateforesight.eu/hp-rewrite/94edef6b5879603d8ff708d4174d83ec)
- 2019-12-15, COP25 Madrid: about 40 to 44 hours late, at the time the longest ever. **Yes.** [The Conversation](https://theconversation.com/the-madrid-climate-talks-failed-spectacularly-heres-what-went-down-128921)
- From memory, unverified:
  - COP24 Katowice (2018): closed late Saturday. **Yes.**
  - COP23 Bonn (2017): closed early Saturday morning. **No.**
  - COP22 Marrakech (2016): closed late Friday or early Saturday. **No.**
  - COP21 Paris (2015): closed around 19:30 on Saturday. **Yes.**
- Rough tally: about 6 or 7 of the last 10 COPs closed more than 24 hours late, and 2 were close to the line (COP26 and COP28). Since 2018 the typical overrun has been 24 to 44 hours, and none has finished on time.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold about COP31 overrunning. None of the market prices you supplied (DOGE, Bitcoin, silver and so on) relates to this question.
- The original Metaculus question (46106) exists, but I did not get its community forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-09: Opening plenaries and agenda adoption. A fight over the agenda would be an early sign of delay.
- 2026-11-11 to 12: Leaders' Summit.
- Around 14 to 15 November: The subsidiary bodies close and ministers take over in the second week.
- 2026-11-19 to 20: Watch when the presidency releases the cover decision drafts, and whether Türkiye and Australia clash over them.
- 2026-11-21 at 18:00 Turkey time (15:00 UTC): the resolution threshold. In Belém, a closing plenary that started after noon on Saturday still ran to about 20:44, so a plenary starting Saturday afternoon could easily end after the threshold.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The outcome should be known about 13 days from now, around 21 to 22 November 2026. For Yes, the last of the COP, CMP and CMA closing plenaries in Antalya must be gavelled closed after 18:00 Turkey time (UTC+3) on Saturday 21 November. That is more than 24 hours after the usual 18:00 Friday finish.

(b) The status quo is that COPs routinely overrun, often closing on Saturday evening or later. Continuing that pattern points weakly toward Yes. It is only weak because Saturday evening sits right on the threshold.

(c) Base rate: Carbon Brief found that 8 of 10 COPs from COP18 to COP27 overran by more than 24 hours. Adding COP28 (probably just under), COP29 (about 30 hours or more over) and COP30 (about 27 hours over) gives roughly 10 of 13, or about 75%. The two COPs under 24 hours in the Carbon Brief count, plus COP28 just under, show that a meaningful share land near the line.
- Several of the "over" cases were only narrowly over: COP21 at about 25 hours and COP30 at about 27 hours.
- So the distribution has a lot of mass close to the threshold.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The persistent overrun habit, including COP29 and COP30 in 2024 and 2025.
- Climate Home's preview (5 November 2026) lists many disputed topics: an agenda fight over the African Group and Nepal items, fossil-fuel language in the cover decision, a number for adaptation finance, the just transition mechanism, AR7 timing and trade.
- The split Türkiye/Australia leadership, with Türkiye insisting on the final say, could add friction in the endgame.

Evidence for No:
- Expectations are low: the EU official's "We cannot expect a revolution" and Carbon Pulse calling Article 6 "low drama" (early November 2026).
- There is no headline finance goal like COP29's NCQG.
- Australia, which is running the negotiations, has an incentive to show efficient management.
- Lower-stakes, implementation-type COPs such as COP22 and COP23 finished under 24 hours late.

(e) No scenario: drafts appear on Thursday and Friday, the remaining issues are modest, and Bowen gavels through the package in the early hours or by Saturday afternoon, roughly 18 to 23 hours late.

Yes scenario: fights over the agenda, fossil-fuel wording and the adaptation finance number drag on, the cover text comes out on Saturday morning as it did at COP30, the closing plenary starts late, and gavelling happens on Saturday night or Sunday.

(f) I start at about 75% and move down to about 62%. The threshold sits right at the modal Saturday-evening closing time, and the agenda looks lower-stakes than COP29's. The split presidency and the many open issues stop me from going lower.

Probability: 62%

**(a) Time left and what Yes requires.** The outcome will be known by about 21 to 23 November 2026, roughly two weeks from now. Yes requires the last of the COP, CMP and CMA closing plenaries in Antalya to be gavelled after 18:00 Turkey time on Saturday 21 November. That is more than 24 hours after the scheduled Friday 18:00 close.

**(b) Status quo.** COPs nearly always overrun, typically into Saturday evening or Sunday. The status quo is therefore an overrun near or past the threshold, which leans Yes.

**(c) Base rate.** Closing times of recent COPs against "Saturday 18:00 local":
- Over the threshold: COP21 (borderline over), COP24, COP25, COP26, COP27, COP29 and COP30 (by about 3 hours).
- Under the threshold: COP22 and COP23.
- Roughly at the 24-hour mark: COP28.

Carbon Brief found 8 of 10 COPs from COP18 to COP27 ran more than 24 hours over. Adding COP28 to COP30 gives roughly 10 of the last 13, or about 70 to 75%.
